root_cause.text: The `skb_header_pointer()` function in the u32 classifier does not fully validate negative offset values, allowing out-of-bounds memory access when a negative offset is passed to it.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces all calls to `skb_header_pointer()` with `skb_header_pointer_careful()` in net/sched/cls_u32.c. The commit message explicitly states "skb_header_pointer() does not fully validate negative @offset values" and the original code at line 164-165 attempted a manual validation check (`if (skb_headroom(skb) + toff > INT_MAX)`) which was insufficient. The KASAN slab-out-of-bounds error at u32_classify+0x1180 confirms that negative offsets were bypassing the inadequate validation and causing memory access violations. The fix uses `skb_header_pointer_careful()` which provides proper validation of offset values to prevent such out-of-bounds access.
